method: Source plan outlines were reviewed in the existing registered building frame. This is coarse exterior massing: door/window gaps are closed, glazing and masonry are not distinguished, small facade returns/columns/entrance canopies are simplified. No room, original wall, height, material or measured thickness is inferred from these profiles.
limitations: Horizontal traces and existing floor registration are approximate; lower-level source clipping, facade recesses, terraces, shafts and renovation currency remain unverified. The 0.5 ft inward shell thickness is display-only. Closed shell surfaces include doors and windows without claiming their locations/materials. This is not an as-built envelope, weatherproofing model, or RF obstruction model. Roofs are removable flat massing caps with 0.5 ft assumed display thickness extending downward from their anchor. Actual roof slopes, pleats, assemblies, penetrations, drains, parapets and landscaping remain unmodeled. Terrace/ground-cover caps close exposed lower profiles without verifying use or grade.

sources.title: UT ECJ roof replacement RFQ and historical record elevations
sources.evidence: The official RFQ distinguishes Level 11 lower roof / mechanical-penthouse floor from the upper penthouse roof. WJE record sheets S3.2/S3.1 reproduced in Sarlo 2018 give lower roof EL 694 and penthouse roof EL 711, relative to Level 1 EL 552: +142 ft and +159 ft. Roof geometry is simplified to registered plan footprints; parapets and buildup are not resolved.

sub-basement.note: Page1 broad podium enclosure, simplified at minor service recesses. Western retaining walls, southern areaway, internal pits and overhead ramp projection are excluded from the exterior massing footprint. Level elevation is unknown.

basement.note: Page2 broader podium outline with north ramp/stair enclosure and south service projection. Open areaway/retaining boundaries are excluded. The northern ramp region is a coarse massing closure; above-grade facade and ground interface remain unverified.

first.note: Page3 first-floor occupied podium perimeter simplified to facade/glazing plane. Open external retaining walls and north ramp/steps are not extruded as enclosed rooms; small entry recesses are simplified. It is deliberately smaller than the basement podium.

typical-tower.note: Pages4–12 repeat the tower facade/glazing plane between projecting corner/edge columns. The complete rectangle is visible on page 4 even though the automatic room detector missed the large northwest lobby. Grid134x102 ft corroborates the scale; tiny column projections/corner chamfers and exterior entrance porch/steps are omitted. These facade dimensions are traced from registered plans, not surveyed.

penthouse.note: Page13 inner wall rectangle around the mechanical spaces is the penthouse facade; its outer nested rectangles are lower-roof/parapet projections and must not become another tall storey. Plan coordinates are approximate registered feet. Page15 roof outline independently follows approximately the same inner rectangle.
